entry.title: Cavtat Beach
entry.summary: Cavtat is a small old town south of Dubrovnik, with rock platforms, small pebble beaches and a long coastal path. The sea is clear, and the Mediterranean pines give shade along the shoreline.

entry.title: Plage de La Grande-Motte
entry.summary: La Grande-Motte is a modern seaside town with a very long beach of fine sand, backed by fenced dunes and the pyramid-shaped apartment blocks of its 1960s architecture. The water is shallow and warm, and it is a family resort in summer.

entry.title: Arvanitia Beach, Nafplio
entry.summary: Arvanitia is a small pebble beach at the foot of the Nafplio fortress hill, reached by a path around the rocks. The water is clear and calm, and the town of Nafplio, with its Venetian old town, is a few minutes on foot.

entry.title: Praia de Espinho
entry.summary: Espinho has a wide beach of fine sand on the Atlantic coast south of Porto, with a long promenade and beach bars. The sea is cool and waves are moderate, and surfers use the north end of the beach.

entry.title: Praia da Figueirinha, Setubal
entry.summary: Praia da Figueirinha is a calm sand beach in the Arrabida natural park, with turquoise water and green hills behind. It is one of the most beautiful beaches near Lisbon, and the road in is limited in summer.

entry.title: Praia Atlantica, Troia
entry.summary: Troia is a long sand peninsula south of Lisbon, with wide Atlantic beaches, white dunes and clear water. It is quieter than the Algarve, the ferry from Setubal takes about fifteen minutes, and dolphins are often seen in the Sado estuary.

entry.title: Vodice Beach
entry.summary: Vodice has several calm pebble and rock beaches around a small harbour town in northern Dalmatia, with pine shade and shallow clear water. It is a family-friendly base and a short boat ride from the islands and Krka waterfalls.

entry.title: Malia Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Malia has a wide sandy beach on the north coast of Crete, with lifeguard stations, sunbeds and mountains behind. Parts of the shore are rocky and wild with dunes, and the Minoan palace of Malia is a short drive away.

entry.title: Kardamena Beach, Kos
entry.summary: Kardamena has a long beach of light sand on the south coast of Kos, with thatched parasols, sunbeds and warm shallow water. The village behind is lively, and boats leave for the volcanic island of Nisyros.

entry.title: Spiaggia Grande, Diamante
entry.summary: Spiaggia Grande is the main beach of Diamante, a pebble and coarse sand bay on the Riviera dei Cedri. The Isola di Cirella sits offshore, the water is clear, and the old town above is covered in colourful murals.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Varazze
entry.summary: Varazze is a Ligurian resort town with a long beach of sand and fine gravel, backed by green hills and a seafront promenade. The sea is clear, the town has a small harbour, and trains from Genoa and Savona stop in the centre.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Punta Aderci, Vasto
entry.summary: Punta Aderci is a protected coastal reserve near Vasto, with beaches of sand and pebbles below low cliffs and wild grass. The sea is clear, there are fewer facilities than on the main Adriatic beaches, and old fishing platforms called trabocchi stand along the coast.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Pescara
entry.summary: Pescara has a wide beach of fine sand running along the city seafront, with long rows of umbrellas and sunbeds and a lively promenade. The water is shallow and warm, and the beach is very popular with Italian families in summer.

entry.title: Ile de Batz Beach, Roscoff
entry.summary: Ile de Batz is a small car-free island off Roscoff, with white sand coves, clear turquoise water and a garden of exotic plants. The ferry from Roscoff takes about fifteen minutes, and the tide can leave long sand flats at low water.

entry.title: Plage de Canet-en-Roussillon
entry.summary: Canet-en-Roussillon is a family resort on the Catalan coast, with a long wide beach of fine sand and the snowy Pyrenees on the horizon. The water is warm and shallow, and the marina and lagoon add watersport options.

entry.title: Plage des Marinieres, Villefranche-sur-Mer
entry.summary: Plage des Marinieres is a small pebble beach in the deep natural harbour of Villefranche-sur-Mer, between Nice and Monaco. The water is very clear and calm, and the old town rises behind in orange and yellow houses.

entry.title: Platja de Malgrat de Mar
entry.summary: Malgrat de Mar has a long beach of coarse sand at the northern end of the Maresme coast, near the mouth of the Tordera river. Its pine campsites and open sections give it a quieter, local feel compared with nearby Blanes.

entry.title: Platja de Pineda de Mar
entry.summary: Pineda de Mar has a long beach of coarse golden sand, with green parkland and pine trees behind and a promenade that runs for kilometres. It is easy to reach from Barcelona by train and is calm and local compared with the busy resorts.

entry.title: Playa de Mojacar
entry.summary: Mojacar Playa is a long beach of sand and fine gravel along the Almeria coast, below the white hill village of Mojacar Pueblo. The sea is clear, the climate is dry and sunny, and the beach is quieter than the big resorts to the west.

entry.title: Playa del Moncayo, Guardamar
entry.summary: Playa del Moncayo is a long beach of fine sand in Guardamar del Segura, backed by high dunes and a pine forest planted to hold them. The water is clear and shallow, and the setting is wilder than most Costa Blanca resorts.

entry.title: Torrevieja Beach
entry.summary: Torrevieja has several sand beaches within the town, with thatched parasols, sunbeds and warm shallow water. It is one of the sunniest spots on the Costa Blanca, and the pink salt lakes are close by.

entry.title: Platja del Morro de Gos, Oropesa
entry.summary: Platja del Morro de Gos is a calm bay of sand and fine gravel in Oropesa del Mar, with clear shallow water. The Morro de Gos headland shelters it, and the old town and castle sit on the hill above.

entry.title: Playa San Antonio, Cullera
entry.summary: Playa San Antonio is a wide beach of fine sand in Cullera, lined with palms and backed by apartment blocks and the hill of the castle. The water is shallow and warm, and the lighthouse hill offers views along the coast.

entry.title: Playa de Gandia
entry.summary: Gandia has one of the widest beaches on the Valencia coast, with fine golden sand, shallow water and a long promenade. It is a lively family resort in summer and calm and local in spring and autumn.

entry.title: Playa de Levante, Santa Pola
entry.summary: Playa de Levante is a long, gently shelving beach of fine sand in Santa Pola, lined with date palms and a flat promenade. The sea is warm and shallow, and the salt lakes and flamingos of the nearby natural park are a short drive away.

entry.title: Platja de Roses
entry.summary: Roses sits on a big, sweeping bay at the top of the Costa Brava, with a long beach of fine sand and calm water. The Cap de Creus natural park and the small cove of Canyelles are a short drive away.

entry.title: Praia da Povoa de Varzim
entry.summary: Povoa de Varzim has a wide, flat beach of golden sand on the Atlantic coast north of Porto, with a casino, promenade and fishing quarter behind. The sea is cool and waves are moderate, so beaches are usually staffed by lifeguards.

entry.title: Plage de Saint-Aygulf, Frejus
entry.summary: Saint-Aygulf is a long, family-friendly sand beach near Frejus, with clear shallow water and a backdrop of pines and the red Esterel hills. It is quieter than Saint-Raphael and Frejus plage.

entry.title: Playa de Moraira
entry.summary: Moraira is a small, upmarket town on the Costa Blanca with a calm sandy cove and an old fishing quarter. The water is clear and sheltered, and the cliff paths lead to small rocky coves nearby.

entry.title: Hersonissos Beach
entry.summary: Hersonissos has a sandy town beach and many smaller coves along the north coast of Crete, with warm clear water and a lively promenade. Mountains rise behind, and the old town of Piskopiano is a short drive up the hill.
